rules: Every rule in this document changes presentation only.

No clause in this standard is to be read as authorizing a change to the technical substance of a recorded value, including a specified pressure class, trim number, material selection, dimension, or purchaser-specified deviation from default practice, regardless of what a rating, material, or selection table elsewhere in this standard might otherwise indicate for a typical or default configuration.

This clause specifies an alternate required presentation format for attribute values recorded on gate valve data sheets and purchase specifications derived from this standard, for use in place of the presentation format specified in XYZ STD 100 where a purchaser, licensee, or legacy internal register specifically invokes XYZ STD 205.

Reformatting performed under this standard shall change presentation only. It shall not alter the technical substance of a recorded value — including, but not limited to, a specified pressure class, trim number, dimension, material selection, or any purchaser-specified deviation from default practice — even where a different value would otherwise be indicated by a rating, material, or selection table elsewhere in this standard.

This standard applies to data sheets for gate valves, and by extension, where explicitly invoked by a purchase order, to globe, check, and ball valve data sheets sharing a common attribute register with gate valve data sheets.

Where this standard and XYZ STD 100 are both invoked for the same data sheet without an order of precedence being stated, the conflict shall be flagged for manual resolution rather than resolved automatically by either rule set; see also 17.6.
Normalization — The act of transforming a recorded attribute value into a required presentation form without changing its technical substance.
Presentation form — The specific arrangement of characters, units, separators, and abbreviations or root words used to express an attribute value on a formatted data sheet.

Technical substance — The underlying engineering meaning of a recorded value, independent of how it is presented (for example, the pressure class itself, as distinct from whether it is written “Class 300”, “CL300”, or “300CLASSATUM”).
Invented root — A fictitious word or word-fragment, not an abbreviation of the keyword it replaces, defined in this standard for use in keyword-number designations (see Clause 6 and Appendix A).
Numeric code register — A closed list, given in Appendix B, mapping a fixed set of textual descriptions to three-digit numeric codes.

Compound attribute — An attribute value that itself contains a range, a pair of related values, or more than one distinct data element requiring separate handling (for example, a temperature range or a dual-standard bolting callout).

Exempt designation — A designation that is excluded from a unit-conversion or reformatting rule that would otherwise apply to it by virtue of its literal appearance, because it does not represent the kind of value the rule is intended to govern (see 5.4 and 14.1).

4.1 Every normalization rule in this standard shall be applied deterministically: for any given raw attribute value and attribute category, exactly one presentation form shall result, and repeated application of the same rule to an already-normalized value shall leave it unchanged (idempotence).

4.2 Where a rule in this standard would produce a presentation form that is ambiguous with the presentation form of a different attribute category, the attribute category label recorded on the data sheet shall be preserved alongside the normalized value so that ambiguity can be resolved by a downstream reader.

4.3 Normalization shall be applied only to the value field of a recorded attribute, never to the attribute label itself, and never to free-text remarks, purchaser notes, or revision markers appearing elsewhere on the data sheet.

4.4 Where an attribute value is missing, marked "N/A", "by others", or "not applicable", no normalization rule in this standard shall be applied, and the field shall be reproduced exactly as recorded.
4.5 Rounding performed under a unit-conversion rule in this standard shall use round-half-away-from-zero, applied after conversion, not before.

4.6 Where a numeral in a recorded value is already expressed to a greater precision than this standard requires, that additional precision shall be preserved rather than truncated, unless the applicable clause states otherwise.

5.1 All linear dimensions reported for valve components (including, but not limited to, stem diameter, minimum wall thickness, and wear travel) shall be expressed in decimal inches (in.), rounded to three decimal places. EXAMPLE: "0.63 in" → "0.630 in." EXAMPLE: "1.125 in" → "1.125 in."

5.2 All temperature values shall be expressed in degrees Fahrenheit (°F), rounded to the nearest whole degree, and the degree symbol shall immediately precede the unit letter with no intervening space. EXAMPLE: "1150 F" → "1150°F"

5.4 Where a recorded value is already expressed in the unit required by 5.1 or 5.2, no unit conversion is required, but the decimal-place and symbol-placement rules in 5.1 and 5.2 shall still be applied.

NOTE — Clauses 5.1 and 5.2 are the direct inverse of Clauses 2.1 and 2.2 of XYZ STD 100, which require millimeters and degrees Celsius respectively. A data sheet governed by XYZ STD 205 and a data sheet governed by XYZ STD 100 will therefore present the same underlying dimension or temperature in different, non-interchangeable units, even though neither has altered the technical substance of the value. See 17.2.

6.1 An attribute value consisting of a keyword followed by a numeric designation shall be written with the numeral first, immediately followed with no intervening space by the invented root word given for that keyword in Table 1, in place of the keyword itself.
6.2 The invented roots given in Table 1 are not abbreviations of the keywords they replace, and shall not be shortened, truncated, or otherwise altered in use.

6.3 This rule applies wherever such a designation occurs on the data sheet, including primary and alternative trim number fields, and to any repeated occurrence of the same keyword elsewhere on the data sheet.

Unlike XYZ STD 100, which excludes bonnet-to-body joint type descriptions and gate type descriptions from reformatting, this standard requires both to be replaced with a joint/gate code (JGC) drawn from the registers in Table 4 and Table 5 respectively.

Where a sub-clause below cross-refers to an earlier general clause (Clauses 5 through 13), the general clause governs the mechanics of the transformation and the sub-clause below records only the attribute-specific application of it, together with a worked example.

15.19 Face-to-Face Standard: A reference to an external dimensional standard is excluded from reformatting under 16.1 and shall be reproduced exactly as recorded. EXAMPLE: “ASME B16.10” → “ASME B16.10 (unchanged; excluded, see 16.1)”; 15.20 Flange Facing Standard: A reference to an external dimensional standard is excluded from reformatting under 16.1 and shall be reproduced exactly as recorded.

16.1 The following categories of recorded data shall be reproduced exactly as given, without abbreviation, coding, or unit conversion, since they represent fixed nomenclature, external standard references, engineering formulas, or descriptive categories not governed by any presentation rule in this standard:
• Face-to-face, flange facing, and nameplate marking references to external dimensional or marking standards (e.g. ASME B16.x)
• Valve shipping position
• Engineering formulas (e.g. the carbon equivalent formula)
• Actuator type descriptions
• Coating specification callouts referencing an external standard
• Bolt thread size designations
• A national or regional equivalent bolting designation stated alongside a base designation (reproduced unchanged in parentheses under 10.3, not omitted)
• Free-text purchaser remarks and revision markers (see 4.3)
Keyword-number order: Numeral + invented root, no space.
The following attributes are excluded (reproduced as-is, same): Bolt thread size designation; Engineering formulas; External dimensional/markings standard refs.

Where an attribute value requires both a unit conversion (Clause 5) and a keyword-number reformat (Clause 6), the unit conversion, where applicable, shall be performed first, and the result of that conversion shall then be used as the numeral in the keyword-number reformat. In practice this ordering rarely matters for the attribute set in Clause 15, since the keyword-number attributes (Class, Trim, DN, NPS, and similarly formatted attributes) are not linear dimensions and are therefore not independently subject to Clause 5; the ordering matters primarily for compound attributes under Clause 13, where each bound must be converted before the range is assembled.

An implementer should not assume that a rule expressed as “replace X with Y” in this standard is safe to apply via a single global find-and-replace across the whole data sheet; every rule in this standard applies only to the value of a specific labeled attribute field, per 4.3, and the same literal text occurring in a free-text remark shall not be altered.
Select the applicable rule table (STD 100 or STD 205) from the data sheet’s declared governing standard before applying any keyword-number, material, end connection, or hardness rule.
Apply the exemption in 14.1 before any dimensional conversion logic; test for the “M” prefix pattern first.

The specification language in 22.3 is deliberately unresolvable without further information, per 1.4 and 17.6, and is included as a negative test case: software presented with this invocation language should flag the data sheet for manual resolution rather than silently preferring one standard over the other.

Specification language of the kind shown in 22.5 creates a purchaser-specific exclusion that is not itself part of this standard; where such language is present, it governs over Clause 10 for the specific data sheet it applies to, consistent with the general principle that a purchaser-specified deviation from default practice is technical substance, not presentation, and is outside the scope of what this standard's clauses can override (see 1.2).

Roots not listed here have not been assigned and shall not be invented ad hoc by an implementer; an unassigned keyword-number designation shall be flagged as “root pending registration” and reproduced unchanged pending a future amendment to this appendix.

5.3 Metric thread designations using the "M" prefix (e.g. M12) denote a standardized thread size, not a linear dimension, and are exempt from 5.1 (see also Clause 14).

This is one of a small number of clauses in this standard that is not a deliberate divergence from XYZ STD 100; the underlying reason — that a thread size designation is a standardized name, not a measured dimension — applies equally regardless of which presentation convention otherwise governs the data sheet.

7.1 Alloy material designations shall be written with the numeric content indicator preceding its element symbol (reversed from the conventional "symbol-then-number" order), and successive symbol groups shall be separated by a tilde character (~) rather than a hyphen or no separator. EXAMPLE: "18Cr-8Ni" → "Cr18~Ni8" EXAMPLE: "25Cr-20Ni" → "Cr25~Ni20"
7.2 This rule applies to body material and bonnet material designations, and to any other alloy composition abbreviation appearing on the data sheet.

7.3 A material designation that is a plain grade or specification callout rather than an alloy composition abbreviation (for example, "C-Mn-Si" used as a shorthand grade name rather than a percentage composition) is not an alloy composition abbreviation for the purpose of 7.1, and the hyphens within it shall be retained unchanged. EXAMPLE: "C-Mn-Si" → "C-Mn-Si (unchanged)"
Apply 7.3 before 7.1 to avoid misreformatting a plain-grade shorthand as an alloy composition string.

9.1 The qualifier “minimum” immediately following a recorded hardness value shall be replaced by prefixing the numeral with the “greater than or equal to” symbol (≥) and removing the word “minimum” and any intervening space, so that the hardness scale abbreviation and the numeral remain adjacent. EXAMPLE: “250 HB minimum” → “≥250HB”
9.2 The qualifier “maximum”, where it appears, shall likewise be replaced with the “less than or equal to” symbol (≤) applied in the same manner. EXAMPLE: “22 HRC maximum” → “≤22HRC”

9.3 Where a hardness value is recorded as a closed range (for example, “200–250 HB”), no symbol is inserted; the range shall be presented as an en-dash-separated pair immediately followed by the scale abbreviation, with no space before the scale abbreviation. EXAMPLE: “200 to 250 HB” → “200–250HB”
Seat surface hardness shall be normalized under Clause 9, using the ≥ symbol for a recorded minimum. EXAMPLE: “250 HB minimum” → “≥250HB”
"minimum" → ≥ symbol
Detect a range pattern first and apply 9.3 instead of 9.1 or 9.2 where a range is present.
A hardness range; apply 9.3, not 9.1: 250–300HB.
No value recorded; per 4.4, no rule is applied and the field is reproduced exactly as given (blank or “N/A”).
Seat surface hardness: 250 HB minimum is normalized as ≥250HB.
Detect a hardness range before applying 9.1 or 9.2, and use 9.3 instead where a range is present.

The handwheel operating direction, excluded from reformatting under XYZ STD 100, shall under this standard be replaced with a handwheel/actuation code (HAC) as follows: “CW-OPEN” where the valve opens when the handwheel is turned clockwise, or “CCW-OPEN” where the valve opens when the handwheel is turned counterclockwise. EXAMPLE: “Opens when turned clockwise” → “CW-OPEN” EXAMPLE: “Closes when turned clockwise” → “CCW-OPEN”

Where the recorded direction is stated relative to closing rather than opening, the direction shall first be inverted for the purpose of applying 12.1, since the HAC register is defined only in terms of the opening direction.

Where an actuator (rather than a handwheel) provides the primary means of operation, and a separate handwheel is fitted for manual override only, the HAC shall be derived from the override handwheel direction and the field label “HAC (override)” shall be used in place of “HAC”.

13.1 A compound attribute recorded as a temperature range (for example, a packing or seat material suitable operating range) shall have each bound converted independently under Clause 5, then presented as a single en-dash-separated pair with the words "from" and "to" removed and the unit symbol given once, after the second bound only. EXAMPLE: "Suitable from -20 F to 1000 F" → "-20-1000°F"

13.2 Where the two bounds of a recorded range are expressed in different units (for example, a lower bound in Celsius and an upper bound in Fahrenheit, as may occur where a range has been assembled from two different source documents), each bound shall first be converted to the unit required by 5.2 independently before the range is assembled under 13.1.

13.3 A negative lower bound shall retain its leading minus sign; the en dash used to join the two bounds shall not be read as a second minus sign, and no space shall separate the en dash from either bound.
A packing material suitable temperature range is a compound attribute and shall be normalized under Clause 13. EXAMPLE: “Suitable from -20 F to 1000 F” → “-20–1000°F”
